sample_unit: scanner log data (examinations and sequences); 4 radiologists rated image quality

links.outcome: Radiologist review of DLR image quality for clinical limitations
links.effect: Radiologists observed artifacts in T2-weighted neuroimaging sequences and reduced quality in contrast-enhanced studies, described as unpredictable performance limiting DLR applicability.
links.quote: Nevertheless, unpredictable performance, particularly in neuroimaging, where artifacts in T2-weighted sequences and reduced quality in contrast-enhanced studies were observed, limits the applicability of DLR and underscores the need for rigorous quality assurance.

unlisted_practices: Simulation-based health technology assessment (Monte Carlo forecast) of productivity gains, validated against post-deployment scanner logs

screen.reason: The study evaluates the operational and productivity impact of deploying deep-learning image reconstruction (DLR) across an MRI scanner fleet, measuring changes in sequence/examination durations and radiologist image quality assessments.
